concepts.description: The drawing names bend, yaw and swivel at the tool-end wrist; radial, rotary and vertical labels describe other depicted motions.

concepts.title: Unimate arm motion labels: In the Unimate drawing, the circular arrow above the rear upright axis is labeled what?
concepts.description: The rear upright-axis arrow is explicitly labeled rotary motion.

concepts.title: Unimate vertical motion: Which association follows the Unimate drawing rather than assuming that every motion label
concepts.description: The drawing labels the angular side-pivot motion as vertical motion; labels describe the pictured result and location, not a universal joint taxonomy.

concepts.title: Modern mobility: Which set contains only forms of modern robot mobility explicitly listed on the slide?
concepts.description: The source names travel on factory floors or uneven terrain and walking, swimming and flying.

concepts.title: Control classification: Which listed classification concerns control rather than mechanical arrangement?
concepts.description: The source labels point-to-point, autonomy and intelligence under control.

concepts.title: Parallel joint labels: Which location–joint pairing matches the parallel-platform drawing?
concepts.description: The figure explicitly labels spherical joints at the top, prismatic action along an extensible leg, and U joints at the base.

concepts.title: Parallel actuation: What does the actuator-motion arrow indicate on the depicted extensible leg?
concepts.description: The paired arrows run along the extensible leg and its prismatic motion direction.

concepts.title: PUMA anatomy: Which ordering follows the labeled PUMA 560 serial mechanism from the base toward the tool
concepts.description: The serial drawing labels waist at the base, shoulder above it, forearm farther along the chain and three wrist rotations at the tool end.

concepts.description: Cartesian, spherical and cylindrical are the three coordinate-based names in the grouped bullet.

concepts.description: The computer-controlled bullet explicitly describes computer inputs often tried in an offline programming system.

concepts.title: Reference-frame change: An unchanged rigid object is described first in frame A and then in frame B; what must cha
concepts.description: A frame determines how position and orientation are expressed; changing reference frame changes the description, not the physical object.

concepts.title: Nearly rigid links: What structural model is used in the manipulator-kinematics slide?
concepts.description: The source describes nearly rigid links connected by joints allowing relative motion of neighboring links.

concepts.title: Higher motion derivatives: Which statement preserves the slide’s stated scope of kinematics?
concepts.description: The source includes position, velocity, acceleration and higher derivatives, and summarizes geometric and time-based properties while excluding force causes.

concepts.description: The slide explicitly describes acceleration in terms of torque and then displacement for the direct problem.

concepts.title: Coordinated joint trajectories: The figure moves the end-effector from A to B while the labeled joint angles change; what
concepts.description: The first bullet says that moving the end-effector from A to B requires computing a trajectory for each joint.

concepts.description: The source contrasts direct trajectory-executing actuators with the majority that supply force or torque and require an effort-computing algorithm.
